reviewer: claude, from frames and the issue text

steps.action: GNOME Settings > Power (Power Mode: Balanced) next to the Resources app showing the Intel i5-10210U processor page with a Temperature graph
rearranges the two windows side by side (until about 00:03.0)
opens the overview; the clip ends

actual: Each time Power Saver is selected, an info row appears under Power Mode: 'Performance mode temporarily disabled due to high operating temperature' (00:05.2-00:12.8 and 00:15.0-00:16.2). The Performance option stays selectable: it is chosen at about 00:14.0 and 00:16.3, and the message disappears when another mode is selected. While the message is shown, the Resources app reads 'Temperature 57 °C · Highest: 93 °C' (00:05.3) and '67 °C · Highest: 93 °C' (00:15.1).
decisive: 00:05.2: right after Power Saver is selected the row 'Performance mode temporarily disabled due to high operating temperature' appears while the CPU temperature reads 57 °C
not_visible: that the machine is not actually overheating - the Resources app shows a momentary 93 °C reading at about 00:01.5-00:02.3 (Highest updates from 82 °C to 93 °C), which a viewer may read as a real high temperature
notes: 1366x768, 21 s. The first 3 s are window rearranging with motion blur. The 93 °C spike in the Resources app is a possible distractor; the current reading is 57-70 °C whenever the message is visible.
